Service Task

General Concept: A Service Task in BPMN is used to perform an automated service, such as calling a web service, executing a script, or interacting with an external system. It is a key element for integrating business processes with IT systems.

 

 

TaktX Implementation: In TaktX, a Service Task is executed by the engine using a configured service handler. You can define input and output mappings using FEEL expressions to transform data before and after the service call. Service Tasks support error handling, retries, and timeouts. Variable scoping ensures that only mapped variables are available to the service handler. The engine supports synchronous and asynchronous execution, and can interact with REST APIs, messaging systems, or custom adapters.

Usage & Options in TaktX:
A Service Task in TaktX allows you to:

  • Configure input and output mappings using FEEL expressions for flexible data transformation.
  • Set up error handling, retries, and timeouts for robust service integration.
  • Service tasks are executed by a job worker; the process always waits for the job worker to report completion before continuing.
  • Integrate with REST APIs, messaging systems, or custom adapters.
  • Limit variable scope to only mapped variables for security and clarity.
  • Monitor execution and audit results via the TaktX client.
  • Attach boundary events for error, escalation, or timer handling.

Example: Automated Invoice Processing with Service Task

 

 

This example shows a process where an invoice is received, an automated Service Task validates the invoice, and then the process continues to either approval or rejection based on the validation result. The Service Task is used for automated validation, demonstrating integration with external systems or microservices.

Tips & Tricks:

  • Use FEEL expressions for flexible data mapping.
  • Configure error handling and retries for robust integration.
  • Limit the scope of variables to only those needed by the service.
  • Document service endpoints and expected responses.

Pitfalls:

  • Unmapped variables will not be available to the service handler.
  • Handle service errors and timeouts to avoid process interruptions.
  • Ensure service endpoints are reachable and properly secured.
